chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil narrated to me, saying: Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari narrated to me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Malik ibn 'Atiyyah, from Minhal al-Qassab, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Whoever recites the Quran while he is a believing youth, the Quran becomes mixed with his blood and flesh, and Allah makes him with the honored, virtuous angels, and the Quran will be an advocate for him on the Day of Resurrection.
And it will say: 'O Lord, indeed every worker has attained the reward of his deed, except my worker; so convey to him the generosity of Your gifts.'
So Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, will clothe him with two garments from the garments of Paradise, and the crown of honor will be placed on his head.
Then it will be said to him: 'Have We satisfied you with it?' The Quran will say: 'O Lord, I desired for him that which is better than this.'
He said: So security will be given to his right and eternity to his left, then he will enter Paradise.
It will be said to him: 'Recite a verse and ascend a degree.'
Then it will be said to him: 'We have conveyed it through him and satisfied you with it,' so he will say: 'O Allah, yes.'
And whoever recites much and is consistent with it due to the strength of his memorization, Allah will give him the reward of this twice.
ai.seo_question: What are the rewards for a young believer who recites the Quran?
ai.summary: In Shia tradition, this hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq emphasizes the transformative power of early Quranic immersion, where the text becomes integral to the believer's very essence ('mixed with blood and flesh'). It details the Quran's active role as an intercessor (hujjah) on the Day of Judgment, securing dual garments of Paradise and a crown of honor, while highlighting that consistent memorization doubles these eschatological rewards.
